sentence: This project designs small molecules that block the entry of coronaviruses, arenaviruses, flaviviruses and filoviruses into cells, as possible antiviral drugs.
This project studies a very short type of tumor DNA in plasma from lung cancer patients, and other molecules, to detect cancer with liquid biopsy.
This project provides mass spectrometry and proteomics services that identify and measure small molecules and proteins, and image tissues, for digestive disease research.
This project builds a viral tool that delivers genes straight into tumor-specific T cells inside the body, without growing the cells outside first.
This project builds a nanocarrier that responds to acidity and carries drugs into bacterial biofilms, so the drugs reach high levels there.
This project studies how a toxin made by Streptococcus pneumoniae damages the lung epithelium and helps the bacteria spread from the lungs to the blood.
This project builds a device that measures epilepsy drug levels in a patient's saliva using chemical sensing, so the dose can be found quickly.
This project studies how drugs that target the capsid of Hepatitis B Virus affect capsid assembly and aggregation.
This project builds software that measures how people move, using a single handheld smartphone, to find changes in movement that could predict mobility decline.
This project uses smartphone tests to study how cognitive problems, negative emotions and social contexts relate to suicide risk in Veterans.
This project tries to find out how branched-chain keto acids help melanoma tumors grow and weaken immune activity near the brain and spinal cord.
This project studies the microbiome in nasal and fecal samples to see how it shapes vaccine response, respiratory infection and asthma.
This project builds a 3D model from human stem cells with open blood vessels to study how amyloid protein buildup harms brain blood vessels.
This project tests whether blocking the protein phosphatase 4 complex during chemotherapy helps ovarian cancer respond better to immune checkpoint blockade.
This project studies the role of the immune system and inflammation in infectious diseases, cancer immunotherapy and muscular dystrophies.
This project builds a data platform that lets researchers share, combine and analyze stroke data from preclinical studies.
This project studies how lipid problems in the glomerular endothelium lead to Alport syndrome, and uses extracellular vesicles as a tool to restore function.
This project uses Patch-seq to study how neurons control axon regeneration in the mammalian spinal cord after injury.
This project studies how synapses form between inner hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons in the inner ear, focusing on synaptic adhesion molecules.
This project supports research in biomedical informatics, the field that uses data, information and technologies to improve health care and biomedical research.
